content:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created by automated monitor — KV-cache partition imbalance causing NCCL stalls and machine-level paging in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-shard-imbalance|kv-shard-imbalance>.

jamie: seeing huge tail latencies and spike in read errors for Dedicated customers on kv-model:open-kv-v2. paging + GPU mem thrash. Starting thread.

neha: ack - I’m oncall. Pinging infra + ml. Any recent config changes?

leo: I rolled a continuous-batching tweak ~55m ago to increase target batch size for that model (target = 1024 -> was 256) to save token-cost.

carlos: infra telemetry shows repeated NCCL TIMEOUTs and NVLINK retries on nodes kv-shard-usw-3/4/7. dmesg shows peer memory errors:
```
[drm] nv_peer_mem: failed to map peer memory region: -110
NCCL WARN Call to cudaDeviceSynchronize() failed: timeout
```

maria: handing off from previous oncall; they flagged increasing swap usage on the worker host at 17:03. Looks like KV cache got unevenly partitioned and some shards blew past memory targets.

jamie: customer impact: CS reported 3 paying customers with >5s median latency and intermittent 500s for generation. Marking affected customers in incident. @cs-ops pls notify.

cs-ops: notified customers A/B/C, explained we’re mitigating and will provide ETA.

neha: hypothesis: larger continuous-batching + TP KV-shard assignment bug caused some partitions to grow without proper eviction -> page to disk -> NCCL stalls when TP tries to sync oversized KV. We should revert batching change and re-balance KV shards.

leo: prepare to revert — config is in git: `infra/configs/serve/kv-open-kv-v2.yaml`. Current change set: `continuous_batching: target_size: 1024`

deploy-bot: deploy queued: Revert continuous-batching target_size to 256 for open-kv-v2. CI quick checks passed.

carlos: while revert deploys, we need immediate mitigation to reduce paging: 1) disable continuous-batching on affected model instances; 2) lower max_batch_size; 3) restart affected shard processes to free cached KV.

neha: commands I’m running now:
```
# disable continuous batching for model on cluster
rdwctl models update open-kv-v2 --set continuous_batching=false --env us-west-2
# lower max batch
rdwctl models update open-kv-v2 --set max_batch_size=128 --env us-west-2
```

leo: also doing rolling restart of nodes with tag kv-shard-usw to clear out stale allocations:
```
for n in $(rdwctl nodes list --tag=kv-shard-usw | awk '{print $1}'); do
  rdwctl nodes restart $n --graceful --wait 30s &
done
```

jamie: applying a temporary placement policy to avoid TP across hosts with high swap: `rdwctl placement set --avoid-tag=high-swap-usw --model open-kv-v2`

carlos: restart hit: nodes 3 and 7 came back with healthy NCCL links. nv_peer_mem errors stopped on those. Node 4 still showing elevated swap, evicting large KV pages.

neha: monitoring: after disabling continuous-batching and lowering max_batch_size we see paging drop ~80% and tail latency improving. CC: latency graphs -> <https://observability/internal/graphs/kv-open-kv-v2?range=15m>.

cs-ops: customers A/B/C updated: "we saw improvement and will follow up when fully stabilized".

deploy-bot: revert deploy to batch config completed and rolled to 6/6 replicas in us-west-2 :white_check_mark:.

maria: good. next: we should rebalance KV partitions proactively to avoid future hot shards. Proposal: change sharding strategy from modulo-round to size-aware hash + soft-evict threshold.

leo: agree. I’ll prototype a safe rollout: 1) enable size-aware sharding in simulator; 2) run canary on 1 shard; 3) validate eviction behavior under synthetic load.

neha: immediate postmortem TODOs:
- create incident page + timeline
- add emergency playbook step to automatically disable continuous-batching if per-shard mem > 85% for 2m
- alert rule for uneven shard occupancy (stddev > 20% across shards)
- identify changes that increased batch target and require canary gate

jamie: assigning action owners: leo -> shard rebalancing PR and canary; carlos -> infra limit/alerts; maria -> postmortem draft and customer summary; neha -> follow-up hotfix automation.

carlos: one more note — we observed one replica hitting swap because its kernel OOM killer was invoked for an unrelated sidecar. We should add cgroups to isolate sidecars from inference process memory. Creating ticket.

neha: current status: mitigations applied, customers notified, latency trending down. Keeping P1 until shard occupancy stabilized for 30m.

jamie: thanks everyone. If latency back to baseline and no paging for 30m we declare mitigated and start post-incident review. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated?false; reason=monitoring window active. Next automated update in 10m.

(ongoing logs and short chatter follow as we watch the rolling restarts and graphs — all actions and commands above are recorded in the incident tracker.)
